ruling.recommended_action: Refund $11.55 to the rider's original payment method; log the RD-7 notification-duty reminder on the driver's route compliance record (no formal warning — first notification-related incident); no driver violation recorded (RD-4 traffic reason on record, F11) and no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The deviation is real and over tolerance: actual 30.6 km against an optimal 22.4 km, +8.2 km, with 8.19 km billed as excess [F1][F4][RD-1]. It is far beyond the 1 km tolerance, so the refund matrix in RD-2 applies [RD-2].

The whole deviation is one off-route segment, 12:23–12:36, 10.28 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, adding 7.52 km and straying up to 2274 m off route [F3]. I read the rider's words in the only pre-segment messages: a 12:05 pickup note giving her location and clothing, and the driver's 12:06 "on my way" reply — neither names a road, a stop or a route, and neither agrees to anything [F7][F8]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so nothing is missing from the conversation [F9]. The driver's explanation, "Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway was crawling, so I went round it", appears only in a statement written after the trip, not in the chat, and there is no call recording; a post-hoc explanation is not notice given before or at the point of deviation [F10][RD-5]. The off-route segment therefore counts, ground consent_after_or_none [F3][RD-5].

No exemption on RD-3 either: the rider named no place and the car made no stop the rider asked for [F7][F8][RD-3]. Deducting exempt km: (8.19 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4101/km = $11.55, the same figure the fare record itself bills as excess distance [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare, the platform fee and the 1.0× surge are not refunded [F5][F6][RD-2].

The trace settles the traffic screen ✓: the KPE congestion (band 2, 10–19 km/h, 11:59–12:36) was active before and throughout the segment, so a traffic reason exists on the replaced stretch and no driver violation is recorded [F11][F3][RD-4]. Under RD-2 that keeps the outcome at refund of the excess distance fare and takes it out of the "no traffic reason" row [RD-2]. Because the refund rests on the driver's failure to inform the rider, the driver also gets the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and the failure is logged on his route compliance record; this is a first such incident, so no formal warning [RD-7].

No profile fact decides anything: the driver has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's flag_account add-on is not engaged [F17][RD-6]. The amount is under $10 in dispute terms and the records are complete (GPS, timestamped chat, fare breakdown), so the system decides the route case following DISP-001's approach [F1][F4][F9][TH-1][TH-2].

segment_findings.reason: The only rider message before the segment is a 12:05 pickup note naming no road, stop or route, and the driver's 12:06 reply is not rider consent; the driver's explanation of the reroute appears only in his post-trip statement with no call recording, so there was no rider agreement before or at the deviation — the 7.52 km added by this segment is not exempt [F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-5][RD-3].

element_findings.reason: I read every message, the driver's statement and the complaint: a waiting note, an 'on my way' reply and a traffic explanation, plus a distance complaint — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: A traffic reason under RD-4 never exempts the segment or changes the refund; it only decides whether a violation is recorded. The rider gave no consent by 12:23:50 on the complete timestamped chat [F7][F8][F9], so the excess distance fare is still refunded [F3][F11][RD-4][RD-5][RD-2].

Whether other expressways were flowing does not matter: RD-4 asks only whether the replaced stretch had an incident or a band 1–2 speed, and the outcome for the money turns on rider notice and agreement, which is absent [F7][F8][F12][F13][RD-4][RD-5].

A post-trip written statement is not notice given before or at the point of deviation, and verbal notice needs a call recording; the record shows neither rider-facing message about the reroute, so consent_after_or_none counts the segment [F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

The driver's own alternative figure of 7.52 km × $1.4101/km ≈ $10.60 is rejected: the formula uses the billed deviation (8.19 km, F4) less exempt km, and the fare record itself quantifies the excess distance billed at $11.55 [F3][F4][RD-2].

The driver's traffic-reason point succeeds only on the violation question, not on the refund: RD-2 still refunds the excess distance fare where the rider was not informed, and RD-7's reminder-and-log applies because the refund rests on that notice failure [F10][F11][RD-2][RD-7].
Not a claim against the outcome; RD-6 is not engaged on 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so no flag_account is added — the profile alone decides nothing [F17][RD-6].

Only partly accepted: the driver's KPE story does not exempt the segment, but the trace settles the RD-4 screen in the driver's favour on the record (band 2 congestion active 11:59–12:36, F11), so no driver violation is recorded — this does not reduce the $11.55 refund [F3][F11][F14][RD-4][RD-2].

The violation half of this claim is rejected: a traffic reason exists on record under RD-4, so the 'no traffic reason' row (which records a violation) is not met; the refund and the RD-7 reminder-and-log still stand [F10][F11][RD-2][RD-4][RD-7].

The rider's clean profile is accepted as credibility only; profile facts never decide the case, so it adds nothing to the amount, which follows from the deviation and the missing consent [F16][F1][F4][RD-2][RD-6].
